vignette: Ahmad, a 22-year-old auditor from a Middle Eastern background, has been struggling with the aftermath of a traumatic rape that occurred six months ago. Working in finance, Ahmad prides himself on his attention to detail and his ability to process complex financial data efficiently. However, since the incident, he finds it increasingly difficult to concentrate on his work, often feeling overwhelmed by intrusive thoughts that disrupt his focus. The evening of the assault is still vivid in Ahmad’s memory. He had been walking home from a friend's apartment late one night when a stranger overpowered him and forced him into an alleyway. The trauma was not only physical but also deeply psychological; it shattered his sense of safety and left him with a profound feeling of vulnerability. In the days following, he found himself reliving the assault in nightmares, waking up drenched in sweat and screaming. Ahmad initially tried to push through these feelings by burying himself in work. He would stay late at the office, immersing himself in numbers and reports, anything to distract from his thoughts. However, his colleagues began to notice that he was less engaged during meetings and often seemed distant. Ahmad's mind would wander off as if haunted by memories of the assault, making it hard for him to participate fully in discussions or complete tasks efficiently. One particular incident at work stands out; while reviewing a financial report, a colleague asked a routine question about an anomaly that appeared in the data. In his head, Ahmad was still reliving the trauma of the alleyway and found himself unable to respond. The anxiety he felt in those moments was overwhelming, causing him to break into a cold sweat and struggle to maintain composure. To cope with the distressing memories, Ahmad has developed strict routines that offer some semblance of control over his life. He avoids walking alone at night and often checks multiple times to ensure doors are locked when home. These rituals provide temporary relief but do little to alleviate the pervasive sense of dread he carries around. Socially, Ahmad withdraws from friends and family, feeling a growing distance between himself and those who care about him. He used to enjoy going out with his friends for dinner or movies, but now even small gatherings are overwhelming. The thought of being in crowded places triggers flashbacks that leave him feeling trapped and helpless. Recently, he canceled plans at the last minute more than once, citing exhaustion or needing time alone. His parents, who live abroad, sense something is wrong but do not know how to help. Ahmad has been experiencing intense guilt over the assault, believing it was his fault for walking home late at night. He constantly questions what he could have done differently and feels ashamed that he did not fight back harder. These thoughts consume him during quiet moments, such as in the early morning hours when insomnia keeps him awake or on public transportation where he can’t escape his own mind. Despite the challenges, Ahmad remains determined to keep pushing forward. He attends support groups for survivors of sexual assault and has started journaling to express some of his feelings and thoughts. Yet, the ongoing impact of the trauma is evident in his day-to-day life: he jumps at sudden noises, avoids certain areas where the attack occurred, and often feels on edge as if danger might lurk around every corner. Ahmad's journey through this trauma has been arduous, marked by moments of intense distress followed by brief periods of relative calm. He continues to navigate his way back to a sense of normalcy, but the shadow of that traumatic night still looms large over his life.
